column1: # vdi-audit-flipy.tsv -- AUDITOR table, 2026-09-12.
# Not part of the frozen measurement set.  Written for one question: is the
# VDI dispatcher's d0 (EmuTOS' flip_y, vdi/vdi_asm.S:124-125) right on the
# paths the four frozen tables do NOT reach -- the error and fallback arms of
# the handlers that raise the flag, plus the three fields commit 675e311 and
# 1eb4e68 changed (vqt_name's 34th INTOUT word, v_dspcur's INTIN[0] write,
# vqin_mode's device modes).
# EmuTOS raises flip_y at nine sites (grep flip_y, pinned tree
# 1a7484ab): vdi_control.c:379 init_wk (opcodes 1, 100), :631 vq_extnd (102),
# vdi_marker.c:49 vsm_height (19), :178 vqm_attributes (36),
# vdi_text.c:678 setup_width_height (12, 107, and 21 via vst_font),
# :1020 vqt_attributes (38), :1058 vqt_extent (116), :1095 vqt_width (117),
# :1173 vqt_fontinfo (131).  NewTOS returns the flag by OPCODE
# (tos-api/src/vdi/mod.rs:413-420), so every handler arm that returns EARLY,
# or that falls back to a default, is a place where the two could disagree.
# That is what this table drives.
# Excluded for the same reasons as the frozen tables: 1, 2, 100, 101 (would
# destroy the workstation the run measures through), 28/31 in REQUEST mode
# (block on the operator), 124/128 (live mouse and keyboard), 109/110/121
# (need MFDB pointers), escape sub 2/3/17 (mode switch / printer).
# opcode

column5: vqt_width char 1, the low end of the font
vqt_width char 300, above last_ade: the INTOUT[0]=-1 arm
vqt_width char -1, below first_ade: the same arm
vst_font face -1, no such face: the fon6x6 fallback
vst_font after vst_point: the vdi_vst_point arm of vst_font
vsm_height at the WORD maximum, clamped to MAX_MKHT
vqt_name element 9, out of bounds: the fon6x6 fallback
vqt_name element 0, not an element either
vqt_width A on a scaled font: the act_siz arm
vqin_mode device 0: INTOUT[0] must stay untouched
vqin_mode string, as the AES left it
vqin_mode string after the REQUEST write
vqin_mode string after the SAMPLE write
vsin_mode device 9, out of range: stores nothing
v_dspcur with no coordinates: writes INTIN[0]=0
